content: Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital is recognized as the largest hospital in the world, spanning an area of 173 acres. It accommodates 3,200 beds and employs a workforce of 6,760 staff members. The hospital is located in Soweto, South Africa, just outside the city of Johannesburg. It is one of the 40 provincial hospitals in Gauteng and operates under the administration and funding of the Gauteng Provincial Health Authorities. The hospital was originally inaugurated in 1941 by Prime Minister Jan Smuts under the name Royal Imperial Hospital, Baragwanath. In 1948, it was renamed Baragwanath Hospital. In 1997, the name Chris Hani was added to honor Chris Hani, a prominent member of the African National Congress (ANC) and the South African Communist Party (SACP), who was assassinated. The hospital serves an extensive patient population, with over 2,000 individuals seeking medical care there on a daily basis. Alarmingly, nearly 50% of these patients are diagnosed as HIV-positive.
